content.value_statement: Competitive strategy can be unclear when market data is scattered. This skill structures competitor analysis, positioning, pricing, and advantage assessment.
actual_capabilities: Applies Porter's Five Forces to assess industry pressure and attractiveness.
Builds positioning maps using customer-relevant market dimensions.
Profiles competitors across product, pricing, go-to-market, strengths, and weaknesses.
Compares pricing tiers and packaging signals across competing offers.
Identifies differentiation options using Blue Ocean and value innovation frameworks.
Defines monitoring cadences for product, market, and performance signals.
limitations: Does not gather private competitor data or bypass access controls.
Requires user-provided market context for accurate recommendations.
Does not replace legal, financial, or investment advice.
May need current market research for fast-changing industries.

use_cases.title: Plan Startup Positioning
use_cases.description: Map direct and indirect competitors, then define a clear market position for an early product.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sales Battlecards
use_cases.description: Summarize competitor strengths, weaknesses, pricing, and likely objections for customer-facing teams.

use_cases.title: Assess Market Entry
use_cases.description: Evaluate industry rivalry, buyer power, substitutes, and beachhead opportunities before entering a new segment.

prompt_templates.title: Map My Competitors
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis with a known market and product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the competitive landscape for [product] in [market]. Identify direct, indirect, and future competitors. Summarize the main customer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Positioning
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of market gaps and differentiation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a positioning analysis for [company] against [competitors]. Use price, complexity, customer segment, and feature depth as possible dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Competitive Intelligence Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced operating plan for ongoing tracking.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a competitive intelligence plan for [company]. Include public sources, research cadence, competitor profile fields, and signals to monitor.

prompt_templates.title: Create Market Entry Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced strategic planning for a new segment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate entry into [market segment] for [company]. Apply Porter's Five Forces, Blue Ocean actions, pricing comparison, and beachhead market selection.

output_examples.input: Analyze competitors for a B2B onboarding platform serving mid-market SaaS companies.
output_examples.output: A structured landscape with direct competitors, adjacent substitutes, buyer power, rivalry intensity, pricing signals, and recommended differentiation themes.

output_examples.input: Create a positioning map for an AI customer support tool.
output_examples.output: A comparison across automation depth and service complexity, with white-space opportunities and assumptions to validate with customers.

output_examples.input: Assess whether we should enter the healthcare CRM market.
output_examples.output: A market entry assessment covering barriers, substitutes, buyer power, regulatory constraints, beachhead segments, and strategic risks.

best_practices: Provide competitor names, target customers, pricing context, and current positioning assumptions.
Validate white-space opportunities with customer interviews before changing strategy.
Refresh competitive intelligence on a recurring cadence, not only during planning cycles.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a feature checklist as a complete competitive strategy.
Do not use private or unauthorized competitor information.
Do not copy competitor messaging without validating customer needs.

faq.question: What does this skill help analyze?
faq.answer: It helps analyze competitors, market forces, positioning, pricing, differentiation, and strategic advantage.

faq.question: Can it perform live market research?
faq.answer: It can guide research and structure findings, but live data depends on the tools and sources available.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it use?
faq.answer: It includes Porter's Five Forces, Blue Ocean Strategy, positioning maps, pricing analysis, and competitive profiles.

faq.question: Is it only for startups?
faq.answer: No. Startups, product teams, consultants, and established companies can use the same analysis structure.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide your product, market, target customers, known competitors, pricing, and any strategic questions.

faq.question: Can it recommend a go-to-market strategy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare entry options, beachhead segments, differentiation paths, and monitoring priorities.
